title: No Lys store is ever lost or emptied silently: a receipt per store, a put-back that removes nothing, and refusals that say what was lost
purpose: On 16 October 2026 the Lys install on Tom's Mac was replaced and lost, without a word from Lys, liminal's grants, the liminal-seats agent's certificate (agent-d3b5f1169f352e59b569dcdec731db2a) and the Mac's runner join. The code at b542ea2e lets that happen at four points: a put-back deletes data/ before renaming the kept copy in (crates/lys/src/identity/upgrade/data_kept.rs:104); a missing grant log, certificate log or machines file is created empty at boot without a word (grants.rs:137-142, certificates_store.rs:204-207, network_store/journal.rs:125-128) and the grant log's identity is re-established at epoch 0 (grant_changes/identity.rs:135-189); install/build.json records binaries and settings but no store's count (upgrade/record.rs:14-29); and every refusal downstream (NotHeld, "the signature does not verify", "names no dialled runner", machine_not_joined) reads as the person's fault. Tom's word of 19 October (12:04): Lys is broken and ruining everything it touches; fix Lys first. This brief carries DIRECTORY-082 R1 (unlanded; C499 and C500 unticked), adds a receipt of every store's count and digest that boot and every identity act check before serving, makes the only way past a shrink a recorded operator act naming the store, keeps the server's and the computer's join records as one set, and makes every refusal a loss causes say so, with when and what to do again.
task: Land DIRECTORY-082 R1's put-back that removes nothing and counts what it moved aside; write a receipt of every store's count and digest outside data/ and refuse, by store name and before serving, any shrink, empty re-creation or changed grant log identity on every boot and identity act, with a recorded operator act as the only way past; keep the join set together and never overwrite a saved join; and make NotHeld, the signature refusal, the runner refusals and the grant stream name the loss and its epoch.

requirements.title: A put-back moves the window's data aside, removes nothing, and counts it (DIRECTORY-082 R1, carried here)
requirements.spec: Behavioural. This requirement is DIRECTORY-082 R1 as written, carried here because it is the first thing that ruins what Lys touches and has not landed (C499 and C500 stand unticked; crates/lys/src/identity/upgrade/data_kept.rs:104 still removes data/ before renaming the kept copy in). WHEN a put-back restores the kept data (swap::back from any forward failure, swap.rs:408-421, and swap::recover while upgrade.json lacks Started, swap.rs:544-549, reached from install.rs:242, install/command.rs:40 and upgrade.rs:340-342), THE SYSTEM SHALL move data/ to data.rolled-back/<rfc3339>/ (the instant the put-back began, RFC 3339 UTC) before the kept copy is renamed into place, and SHALL remove nothing under data/; the move is a rename within the install root, a name already taken is refused by name and nothing is moved. THE SYSTEM SHALL then print the folder and, for each store under it, the store's name and its count of records, read from the store's own head (FileLeafStore::open_read_only, crates/lys-log-store/src/file.rs:243, and the record count of each one-file store) without reading its history; a store it cannot count is named with the reason, never skipped. data.rolled-back is never pruned by the installer. The kept copy in data.previous stays, as restore keeps it today. The same put-back records the rollback in the acceptance file R2 names (store, count before, count after, at), so the server's next boot refuses the shrunk stores by name until an operator accepts the loss. C499 and C500 are ticked by this brief's lane when its acceptance proves them; DIRECTORY-082's rows are not duplicated.
acceptance: A put-back leaves data/ under data.rolled-back/<rfc3339>/ byte for byte as it stood, and removes no file under data/ (DIRECTORY-082's acceptance, in crates/lys/src/identity/upgrade/data_kept_tests.rs)

The put-back's output names the folder and one record count per store; after writes in the window and a put-back, the previous build reads every pre-window record and every window record is found and counted in data.rolled-back
A taken data.rolled-back name is refused by name and moves nothing
The put-back writes one rollback entry per store whose count shrank into the acceptance file, read back in the test

requirements.title: A receipt names every store's head; boot and every identity act refuse a lost, re-identified or foreign store by name; a store that may shrink honestly is compared by head, never by size; a refused boot says why on /health and the sign-in page
requirements.spec: Behavioural. The receipt is one file outside data/, install/stores.json beside install/build.json (Layout::install_dir, crates/lys/src/identity/install/layout.rs:142-149), with one entry per store: name, the head it is compared by, a digest, read_at, and the store's class (whole or own, below). Its shape lives once, in crates/lys-identity/src/stores_receipt.rs, used by the server and the lys binary both (both depend on lys-identity). How each store is compared is decided here, per store, because a count that may fall honestly must never refuse a boot: (a) an append-only log (the directory log, the organisation configuration log, the grant log, the certificates log, requests, mcp requests, and every lys-log-store store routes_startup.rs:93-128 opens) is compared by head: its origin digest and its head index (FileLeafStore / frontier_log len, crates/lys-log-store/src/frontier_log.rs:217); a head below the receipt's, or another origin, is a loss; a head at or above it with the same origin is fine; (b) a live set whose size falls by design (SpiceDB relations on every revoke; the stores machines, roles, provisioning, apps, homes, runtime, service accounts, reviews, teams, stops, budgets, policies, whose records retire and will be pruned) is never refused for a fall that an acceptance or a recorded removal explains: these stores are FileLeafStore logs in the tree (not one-file journals as this brief first said), and network_store/journal.rs read's third value is a count of entries replayed since the snapshot, not a sequence that only rises, so they are compared by record count against the receipt, with their format digest recorded but not compared because the format moves on first write; (c) SpiceDB is a projection of the grant log, named permission-projection in the receipt (the installer's word filter breaks an accept-loss command that contains the engine's name), and it is compared by the grant-log revision it has projected (grants.rs:88 require_model and :121 hold_model carry a model revision; the projected grant revision is recorded beside it) against the grant log's head. The comparison runs when the grants first open, never at boot: three contracts say a boot never reaches the permission engine (the_health_route_asks_no_other_service, configured_projection_is_reported_without_reading_its_key_or_connecting, and the engine-counter test), and they stand. Behind is projected forward from the log by the server's own projection path (GrantState open with Relationships::SpiceDb, grants.rs:131-150, and lys-identity's projection rebuild, grants/projection_live.rs:105) before anything is judged; ahead of the head, or a projection of another log identity, refuses every grant act by name (spicedb_projection_foreign, naming both revisions and the accept-loss command) while the boot itself serves, so Lys stays up and every refusal says the road out; (d) the install's own files, keys/service.key's and keys/runner-machine.key's public halves, run/runner-join.json, run/runner-server.pub and the data/runner/ owners directory, are compared by digest, presence only (a present receipt entry with the file absent is a loss). An act that legitimately removes records, today none in the tree (no prune or compaction removes a record from any store at b542ea2e; goals compaction_holders is not one), and from now every prune, compaction or retirement that Tom's store-growth work lands, updates the receipt in the same durable operation that removes them, through the one function crates/lys-identity/src/stores_receipt.rs exports for it; a removal that bypasses it is a loss at the next boot, which is the point. The grant log's entry also carries the identity and epoch grant_changes/identity.rs records; another identity is refused (grant_log_identity_changed, naming both). A test fails when a store opened in routes_startup.rs has no entry and no class. The server writes the receipt after its boot check, after every removal (above) and at clean stop, each in one durable write (write, fsync, rename); the lys binary never writes it. Scope of a refusal, decided per store with the reason: a loss of a WHOLE store refuses the boot, because every route depends on it and serving without it would answer wrongly to everyone: the directory log (every identity), the grant log and its identity (every permission), the certificates log with agent-keys (every agent signature), the organisation configuration log (zones and sign-in) and keys/service.key (signs every receipt, join and certificate); a foreign permission projection is not a boot refusal but refuses every grant act, as (c) says. A loss of an OWN store refuses only its own routes, with the loss sentence of R4, while every other route serves, because a convenience store must never take Lys down and the person needs Lys up to repair it: machines with network.joins.json (the network routes and starts on machines refuse; people still sign in and reconnect computers), roles, provisioning, apps, homes, runtime, service accounts, reviews, teams, stops, budgets, policies, requests, mcp requests, and the runner's own files. At boot, before open_directory (routes_startup.rs:93), the server reads the receipt and compares every store it is about to open: a whole store lost (head below, origin changed, identity changed, or a counted store absent) refuses the boot; an own store lost is recorded and its routes refuse from then on. A counted store that is absent is never created empty: grants.rs:137-142, certificates_store.rs:204-207, network_store/journal.rs:125-128 and identity.rs establish's minting at epoch 0 run only for a store the receipt does not name. A refused boot is not Lys down silently: the server binds its listener and serves exactly two things, GET /health (health_api.rs:36), which answers refused_to_start with the store, what the receipt holds and what was found, the exact command (lys identity accept-loss --store <the store named>) and the computer to run it on (this host's name), and the sign-in page (surface/identity/src/features/sign-in/SignIn.tsx), which reads /health and shows those words instead of the form; every other route answers 503 with the same words; the startup lines say the same by store name. The only way past a loss is the recorded operator act: lys identity accept-loss --store <name> [--store <name>]..., which appends to install/stores.accepted.json one entry per named store (store, what the receipt held, what was found, at, the login's user name) and prints each; a store not named is not accepted. At the next boot a store with an acceptance newer than the receipt's read_at is served at what was found, the receipt is rewritten to it, and the acceptance's at becomes that store's loss epoch (R4). Starting a store empty is the same act at nothing found; there is no flag, environment variable or configuration key that skips the check. The lys binary makes the same comparison, for the stores it can read read-only, in every identity act (install, upgrade before data is kept, put-back, recover, stop, start) and refuses by the same names before changing anything. The receipt and acceptance file paths are two new server configuration keys written by the installer (install/server_config/rendering.rs, read in crates/lys-identity-server/src/config.rs); a missing key is written into the configuration by the program that reads it, never defaulted in code (Tom, 12 October 2026).
acceptance: Red first, in a new crates/lys-identity-server/src/../tests/stores_receipt.rs against the crate's server fixture: after grants, a certificate and a machine join are written and the server stops, (a) data/ replaced by an empty directory makes the next boot refuse naming the directory log, the grant log and the certificates store as whole stores, creates no empty store, and serves GET /health as refused_to_start with the store, the receipt's head, what was found, the accept-loss command and this host's name, and the sign-in page's words say the same while every other route answers 503 with them; (b) the grant log truncated by one leaf by the test's own fixture makes the next boot refuse naming grant-log with both heads; (c) a grant log identity file rewritten makes the next boot refuse grant_log_identity_changed naming both identities

In the same file, honest shrink: a revoke that lowers the SpiceDB relation count, then a boot, serves; a projection behind the grant log's head is projected forward when the grants first open and the next grant check serves; a projection recorded at a revision ahead of the head, or under another log identity, makes every grant act refuse spicedb_projection_foreign naming both and the accept-loss command while /health and sign-in serve; a record removed from a store through the receipt's removal function, then a boot, serves, and the same removal made without it is refused at the next boot naming the store (the prune test, driven through the one road every prune must take). The projection legs are proven at unit level (compare_projection) because the harness has no live engine; the live-engine proof is owed at install: the install walk replaces Lys's projection on purpose and reads the refusal and the accept-loss road live, and C777 and C778 are ticked on that walk, not before

In the same file, scope: the machines file absent with every whole store intact boots and serves sign-in, /me and grants; GET /network and a start on a machine refuse with the R4 loss sentence; after accept-loss --store network the next boot serves them
In the same file: an acceptance entry for exactly the named store lets the next boot serve it and rewrites the receipt; a store not named in the acceptance still refuses

In crates/lys-identity/src/stores_receipt_tests.rs: the receipt round-trips, a write is one rename, every store routes_startup.rs opens is named with a class (the test lists them from the server's own store-opening table), and the per-store comparison rules above are each exercised (head below, same head other origin, head above, projection behind, projection ahead, digest presence)

In a new crates/lys/src/identity/upgrade/stores_receipt_tests.rs: lys identity install and upgrade on a root whose receipt names a store the disk lacks refuse by store name and change nothing; accept-loss writes exactly the named entries and prints them

gate -stages nextest -crates lys-identity-server,lys-identity,lys -test 'package(lys-identity-server) | package(lys-identity) | package(lys)' green, counts in the report; surface/identity typecheck, biome and vitest green for SignIn.tsx

requirements.title: The server's join records and the computer's saved join are one set: kept, moved and restored together, and never overwritten under a saved join
requirements.spec: Behavioural. The join set is keys/service.key, run/runner-server.pub (the service key's public half, which install.rs:261-262 writes from service_key(layout) through start_runner), keys/runner-machine.key, run/runner-join.json (crates/lys/src/commands/runner_join.rs:86), data/network.json and data/network.joins.json (network_join.rs:181-183), and data/runner/. An upgrade's keep (data_kept.rs keep) copies the whole set beside data.previous, and a put-back (R1) moves and restores the whole set together, so a machine's record on the server and the computer's saved connection to it never come from two different moments. start_runner (install.rs:168-188) writes run/runner-server.pub only when no run/runner-join.json exists on this computer; where one exists, the install refuses runner_join_present, naming the file and the server it joins, and changes nothing: a computer that joined another Lys is never silently turned into a server of its own. keys/service.key is never regenerated where one exists (load_or_generate, install.rs:119, kept); where the receipt (R2) counts a service key and none is on disk, the install refuses store_missing naming keys/service.key instead of minting one, because every joined computer's saved runner-server.pub names the old key.
acceptance: In crates/lys/src/identity/upgrade/data_kept_tests.rs: after a keep and a put-back with writes to network.json and a new join code in the window, network.json, network.joins.json, run/runner-join.json and run/runner-server.pub are all from the kept moment, and the window's copies are all under data.rolled-back

In a new crates/lys/src/identity/install/runner_join_guard_tests.rs: lys identity install on a root holding run/runner-join.json is refused runner_join_present naming the file and the server, and run/runner-server.pub is byte for byte as before; a root with no saved join writes it as today
In the same file: a root whose receipt counts keys/service.key with the key removed is refused store_missing naming keys/service.key, and no key is generated

requirements.title: Every refusal a lost store causes says so, with when, and what to do again; the grant stream resets a client whose log was rolled back
requirements.spec: Behavioural. The server holds, from the acceptance file (R2), each store's loss epoch: the at of its newest acceptance. While a store has a loss epoch, the refusals its loss causes carry one more sentence naming it: NotHeld from the grant check (grants.rs:263-267) ends "Lys lost its grant records at <rfc3339>; ask for the grant again"; AgentSignatureRefused's "the signature does not verify" (agent_signature.rs:106-111), when the certificates store has a loss epoch, ends "Lys lost its certificate records at <rfc3339>; issue the agent's certificate again"; runner_dial_refused's "names no dialled runner" (runner_dial.rs:85 and :204) and the runner view GET /network/machines/{id}/runner, when the machines store has a loss epoch, carry lost_at, and machine_not_joined at crates/lys/src/commands/launch_device.rs:185-188 ends "Lys lost its computer records at <rfc3339>; connect this computer again" when the view carries it; the earlier machine_not_joined at :91-94 (no key on this device) has read no runner view and carries no sentence. The sentence is added to the words, never in place of the refusal's name, and is absent for a store with no loss. Accepting a loss on the grant log replaces the grant log identity through grant_changes/identity.rs reset (the next epoch, naming the one it replaces), and grant_changes/stream.rs answers a request whose log names the same identity at an earlier epoch with ChangeFrame::Reset{reason: Rollback, from: the asked log}, not OtherLog, whether or not the head has since grown past the request's cursor (today Rollback is answered only while after > head, stream.rs:155-161, so a client that slept through a put-back and new appends resumes a cursor into a log that is not the one it read).
acceptance: In crates/lys-identity-server/tests/stores_receipt.rs: after an accepted loss on the grant log, a check for a grant written in the window is refused NotHeld with the loss sentence and its rfc3339; the same check on an install with no loss carries no such sentence

In the same file: after the accepted loss and three new appends, a grant-changes request naming the old epoch with a cursor below the new head is answered Reset{Rollback} naming the asked log; a request naming the new epoch is answered from its cursor
In the same file: an agent whose certificate was in the lost window is refused with the certificate loss sentence; a machine whose join was in the lost window answers lost_at in its runner view
In crates/lys/src/commands/launch_device_tests.rs: a runner view carrying lost_at makes machine_not_joined end with the computer loss sentence

requirements.title: ADR-114 says what the code does
requirements.spec: Documentary. ADR-114's decision (docs/design/decisions.json) says an upgrade never touches data and that the previous build comes back; since DIRECTORY-045 R7 and DIRECTORY-082 the upgrade keeps data/ whole in data.previous and a put-back restores that copy, and from this brief a put-back moves the window's data to data.rolled-back, removes nothing, and the server refuses to serve a shrunk or missing store until an operator accepts the loss by name. The ADR's decision text is amended to say exactly that, in one added sentence after "Data, credentials, configuration and the compose services are never touched by an upgrade", and a consequence is added: "A put-back never loses a record silently: the window's data is kept beside the install and every shrunk store is refused by name until accepted." DESIGN.md is re-rendered by render-cluster.py so its ADR-114 line (docs/design/directory/DESIGN.md:74) matches. Nothing else in the ADR changes. For Waffles, not for the lane: C393 and the structure rows at DESIGN.md:700 and :792 name `lys identity upgrade --back`, crates/lys/src/identity/upgrade/back.rs and upgrade_back_tests.rs; none of the three is in the tree at b542ea2e and cli.rs has no --back, so those rows describe work that never landed.
acceptance: docs/design/decisions.json ADR-114 carries the added sentence and consequence; python3 scripts/design/validate.py docs/design/decisions.json prints no violation
sh scripts/design/gate.sh prints no 'rendered markdown differs' line for docs/design/directory

boundaries: No store is ever created empty, re-identified or served short of its receipt without a recorded operator act that names it; no flag, environment variable or configuration key skips the check

No store is compared by the size of a live set: append-only logs by head, projections by projected revision, sets by journal head and digest; a boot never refuses an honest shrink (revoke, prune, retirement recorded through the receipt)
A refused boot is never silent: /health and the sign-in page say the store, both heads, the command and the computer; losing an own store never takes Lys down
The installer prunes nothing: data.previous and data.rolled-back stay until a person removes them
The receipt is written only by the server, in one durable write; the lys binary reads it and writes acceptances only
No fixed wait, timer, poll or deadline anywhere, in code or test (Tom, 15 October 2026)
No store's format moves: the receipt sits beside the stores and reads their existing heads
Nothing installed by the lane; every file touched stays under 500 code lines (ADR-111, by scripts/file-length.sh)
verification: gate -stages clippy, then the whole declared gate
sh scripts/design/gate.sh read for FAIL and 'rendered markdown differs' lines (DESIGN.md re-rendered for R5)
python3 scripts/design/validate.py docs/design/directory and python3 scripts/design/check-coverage.py docs/design/directory read for FAIL lines

amendments.by: Waffles (the decision) and Flapjack (the text), on the 4c4b8a09 handback
amendments.subject: The permission projection is compared when the grants first open, never at boot; four other places the tree contradicted the brief
amendments.ruling: The lane found three contracts that forbid a boot reaching the permission engine, and kept them: the projection comparison runs when the grants first open; behind is projected forward before anything is judged; ahead or foreign refuses every grant act spicedb_projection_foreign naming both revisions and the accept-loss command while the boot serves. Accepted, and better than the brief's boot-refusal: Lys stays up and every refusal names the road out. C777 and C778 are ticked only on the live-engine proof, which is the install walk (replace the projection on purpose, read the refusal and the accept-loss road live), not a unit test. Also recorded so the brief says what the code does: the stores this brief called one-file are FileLeafStore logs; journal.rs read's third value is a replay count, so those stores compare by record count with the digest recorded, not compared; machine_not_joined at launch_device.rs:91-94 has no runner view and carries no loss sentence, only :185-188 does; the projection store is named permission-projection. Lesson kept: red first is not optional even when the code seems obvious; R2 and R4's first run found three real defects a red-first run would have caught one step earlier.
